name: Decon-dustrial
summary: Decon-dustrial, also known as Deconstructivist Industrial, is an architectural design from the late 1980s through the early 2000s.
description:
Decon-dustrial, also known as Deconstructivist Industrial, is an architectural design from the late 1980s through the early 2000s. It blends heavy industrial, raw elements with the fragmented, warped, and chaotic geometric shapes of architectural deconstructivism, featuring it with a factory-turned-sci-fi-ruin jagged, unpolished, heavily textured, rusted iron, exposed concrete, steel, cold-rolled distressed brick, and rough-hewn timber. Some components include jumbled metal beams, skewed angles, and non-linear, intersecting structures, exaggerated joints, bolted plates, raw cables, visible welds, and left out in the open where an open-ended, unfinished look feels like a space frozen mid-collapse or mid-construction.

For places, it incorporates alternative clothing stores, trendy urban coffee shops, and industrial loft conversions that utilize exposed ductwork, and jagged metal retail racks, underground club flyers, industrial video games, and heavy-tech graphic design from the early digital era.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Constructivism
